rationale: Evidence: all 60 development trials across iterations 0-2 went off track, with progress of 0.04-0.24. Max error sits at about 0.06, which is the off-track floor, while rms error stays around 0.024-0.03. Steering oscillation is low (0.06-0.16), so the robot is not jittering. It drifts steadily off the line, and ki=0.5 with kp=3 gave the best score so far (69.5), which points to a steady bias that proportional action alone does not hold. Widening the body does not help: the limit is max(0.06, 0.0125+body_width/4), and at body_width 0.18 that is still 0.0575, so the 0.06 floor stays in force. Changes: (1) raise kp from 3.0 to 4.0 for stronger correction through bends; (2) raise ki from 0.5 to 1.0 to remove the residual offset faster (the integral is capped at +/-2, so windup is bounded); (3) raise kd from 0.3 to 0.5 to damp the larger kp, since oscillation is currently low; (4) lower base_speed from 1.0 to 0.9 so the robot has more time to correct at bends. Completion time will suffer, but off-track failure dominates the score; (5) move the sensor row forward from y=0.05 to y=0.08 so the line is seen earlier and the controller leads the bends; (6) narrow wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10 so the same PWM differential gives a sharper turn rate; (7) reduce mass from 0.6 to 0.5 kg to cut yaw inertia. Hypotheses: (a) rms_error falls below 0.02 and max_error stays under 0.05; (b) progress on the s-bend exceeds 0.4; (c) steering_oscillation stays below 0.2 with the higher kp and kd. If oscillation rises, kd is the next lever. If the run completes, raise base_speed to bring completion_time under 3 s. Expected result: fewer off-track exits and progress well above the previous 0.14-0.24.
